back: The variety of life in an area: variety of species, of genes within species and of habitats.
Richness: the number of species. Evenness: how equally individuals are shared between species.
D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², where n is the number of one species and N is the total; 0 = no diversity, near 1 = very high.
Density = individuals ÷ area sampled. Frequency = quadrats containing the species ÷ total quadrats × 100.
Choose sites, place quadrats at random, use enough quadrats, record species and counts, calculate density, frequency and Simpson's index.
